confirmation: Project owner confirmed these results were tested separately in a cloud environment; updated 2026-10-04. Current local regression runs are recorded separately.

experiences.title: AdPulse — Versioned Streaming Measurement and Bounded Query Backend
bullets: Completed a simulated full reconciliation over 3,949,000 synthetic advertising records, comparing receipt, disk-reference and database business results by business key and value: 0 unmatched rows and 0 duplicate business effects; intermediate event row counts are not required to equal the final association count.

Cut the median first-page query time from 622 ms to 32.9 ms (94.71% lower) in an independent 21,667-association, limit-100 experiment pinned to ClickHouse 24.8 and Python 3.12, by pushing filtering and keyset pagination into SQL instead of loading the full association set into Python.

Lowered the traced Python peak allocation for that first page from 71,300,000 B to 399,000 B (99.44%, decimal MB, not RSS) over five alternating paired runs after warmup; timing runs from query-function entry to result-object return and excludes ASGI and JSON serialization.

Pinned pagination to immutable releases with HMAC cursors binding release ID, filters, sort keys and original expiry: traversed 44 pages (43×500 + 167 = 21,667 associations) across 21 active-pointer switches with no missing or duplicate rows, and returned 503 after expiry with no renewal.

Cut median reference-process peak RSS from 1,100,000 KiB to 139,700 KiB (87.3% lower) on 206,000 synthetic records in a fixed 2 CPU / 4 GiB environment using SQLite disk-backed joins and sorting, trading 2.29x elapsed time (32.0 s to 73.28 s, cold index build included) and 605 MiB temporary disk for the memory reduction, with identical output hashes in 3/3 paired runs.

Verified collector admission with a 50-request barrier stress test (1 admitted, 49 rejected) and 9/9 independent health probes, and confirmed that a fenced producer stops admitting input, explicit replacement restores it, and cancellation does not release a running native transaction early.
limits: 32.9 ms excludes ASGI and JSON serialization (it measures query-function entry to result-object return) and is not a user-side P95; 399,000 B is a tracemalloc peak reported in decimal MB, not RSS or total-system memory.

The 87.3% reduction is the 206,000-record reference process on a fixed 2 CPU / 4 GiB share, not Flink or whole-system memory; its costs are 2.29x elapsed time and 605 MiB temporary disk, so it must not be presented as a free win.
Release pinning is an application-level immutable snapshot, not database MVCC; a recycled old release refuses further pagination, and expired cursors return 503 without renewal.

3.8M is the old export (3,833,704 records) and 3,949,000 is the corrected new round; the two sets must not be mixed. The old round's 36.6 ms / 0.443 MB / 200,000-record figures are separate and must not be reused for the new round.

Reconciliation compares receipt, disk-reference and database results by business key and value (0 unmatched, 0 duplicate business effects); it does not assert that intermediate event row counts equal final association counts.

New-round figures come from separate independent experiments with different denominators and pinned versions (8-core/32 GiB Linux; Java 17, Flink 1.20.5, Kafka 3.9; ClickHouse 24.8 in the page experiment, with the post-maintenance 26.3 line verified separately); no production, managed-cloud, HA or multi-host claim.
Collector admission is per process, and native transaction cancellation is not preemptive; the 50-request barrier result is a single local run, and producer replacement is explicit and manual.
